findings.title: Migration aborts when the embed_category or uncategorized row is absent
findings.description: `execute(...)[0]['id']` (line 11) assumes the `INNER JOIN` between `categories` and `site_settings` returns a row. When it returns none, `[0]` is nil (or raises), so `['id']` fails and `db:migrate` stops. Rows in `site_settings` exist only for admin overrides, so an install that never changed `embed_category` has no row and crashes on upgrade. A fresh database has no categories and no settings rows, so the same thing happens there. This repo has no `db/schema.rb` or `db/structure.sql`, so the test database is built by running migrations and the suite cannot be set up. The fallback at lines 14-16 has the same `[0]['value']` problem. `category_id` is `NOT NULL`, so the migration needs an explicit fallback (for example, skip the host insert with a logged warning when no category resolves). It should not raise.

findings.title: Legacy host values are inserted without normalization
findings.description: Each entry from the old `embeddable_hosts` setting is inserted verbatim. The model's `before_validation` (app/models/embeddable_host.rb:5-8) strips the scheme and path, but raw SQL bypasses it. `record_for_host` compares `uri.host` (no scheme) against the stored value, so an entry saved as `http://eviltrout.com`, or with stray whitespace, silently stops matching and that site loses embedding. The old code tolerated scheme-prefixed entries; the deleted `site_setting_spec.rb` cases covered `http://` and `https://` values. Normalize each entry in Ruby (strip whitespace, remove scheme and path, downcase) and skip blanks before inserting.

findings.title: String-interpolated SQL in the migration
findings.description: `VALUES ('#{h}', ...)` interpolates admin-entered text into SQL. A value containing `'` breaks the migration, and a crafted value is SQL injection, although the input is admin-only. Use `connection.quote(h)` or a bound statement.

findings.title: Nil host crashes validation instead of returning a validation error
findings.description: `self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError` when `host` is nil. `save_host` assigns `params[:embeddable_host][:host]` without a guard (app/controllers/admin/embeddable_hosts_controller.rb:23), so a POST or PUT with no `host` returns a 500 rather than the 422 that `render_json_error` would produce. `sub!` also mutates the attribute string in place. Use `self.host = host.to_s.sub(...).sub(...)`.

findings.title: Unknown ids in update and destroy return 500s
findings.description: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id. `update` passes nil into `save_host`, where `nil.host=` raises. `destroy` calls `nil.destroy`. Use `find`, which raises `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` and gives a not-found response instead of a `NoMethodError`.

findings.title: Port is accepted by validation but ignored by matching
findings.description: The regex allows `:port` (`(:[0-9]{1,5})?`) and stores it, but `record_for_host` matches `uri.host`, which never contains a port. A host saved as `example.com:8080` will never match any referer. The old code had the same mismatch, but the new validation now advertises port support. Either reject ports in the validation or match host plus port. The TLD rule `[a-z]{2,5}` also rejects longer TLDs such as `.community`, and it is new behavior that the release notes should mention.

findings.title: Host lookup is case-sensitive on the Ruby side
findings.description: The SQL uses `lower(host)`, but `host` from `uri.host` is never downcased before the comparison. A referer or `embed_url` with an uppercase host (`http://EvilTrout.com/x`) fails to match `eviltrout.com`. `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` passes the raw `embed_url` with no normalization, even though `TopicEmbed.normalize_url` downcases on import. The old code was also case-sensitive, but the new query shows the intent to be case-insensitive. Fix with `host = uri.host.downcase`.

findings.title: No uniqueness, no category check, no index
findings.description: Nothing prevents the same host from being saved twice (no `validates :host, uniqueness`, and no unique index in the migration). Duplicates make `record_for_host` return an arbitrary `.first` with no ordering, so the category chosen for a host is nondeterministic. `belongs_to :category` in this Rails version does not require the category to exist, so a nonexistent `category_id` is accepted. `TopicEmbed` then passes it to PostCreator, where `Category.find_by(id:)` returns nil (lib/topic_creator.rb:117-118). The lookup runs on every embed request with no functional index on `lower(host)`; the table is small, so the cost is low. Add uniqueness on `lower(host)` and a category presence or existence check.

findings.title: PUT /admin/customize/embedding is a silent no-op, and saveChanges is dead code
findings.description: `update` renders the current state and ignores the request, so a PUT returns success and changes nothing. The Ember action `saveChanges` (app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-embedding.js.es6:5-7) calls `update({})` on it, but nothing in `embedding.hbs` binds to that action. Implement the save or remove the route and action until there is something to save.

findings.title: Test name describes behavior that no longer exists
findings.description: "is false if embeddable_host is blank" no longer exercises any host configuration. The topic is unsaved and `has_topic_embed?` is not stubbed, so the assertion passes only because there is no `TopicEmbed`. Delete the test or rename it to what it actually covers.

findings.title: Store test requests id 2 but the mock always returns apple
findings.description: The `/fruits/:id` mock ignores the id and returns `fruits[0]` (apple, `color_ids: [1,2]`). The test's assertions pass against apple's data, so it looks like banana (color 3) is covered when it is not. Read `request.params.id` in the mock, or request id 1.

findings.title: New admin endpoints and UI have no behavior tests
findings.description: Both new admin controller specs only assert class inheritance (`Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController`). Nothing covers create, update, or destroy, the 422 path, non-staff access, or the embedding `show`. The embeddable-host component (add, save, delete, cancel) has no JS test either. The embed controller and model specs are good; the admin surface is uncovered.

findings.title: Fabricators are in the wrong files
findings.description: The `:embeddable_host` fabricator sits in `category_fabricator.rb`, and the category fabricators (`:category`, `:diff_category`, `:happy_category`, `:private_category`) were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`, which I confirmed by reading both files. It works at runtime because Fabrication loads every file, but a reader looking for `:category` will not find it where the name suggests. Swap the contents back.

findings.title: Delete failures are unhandled
findings.description: `destroyRecord().then(...)` has no `.catch(popupAjaxError)`, unlike `save()` at line 40. A failed delete becomes an unhandled promise rejection and the user sees nothing. Add the same catch.

findings.title: `basePath` hack compensates for inconsistent type names in the store
findings.description: `type.replace('_', '-')` exists because `_hydrateEmbedded` and `_lookupSubType` pass underscored names such as `embeddable_host` into `_hydrate`, `_build`, and `adapterFor` (store.js.es6:182). Everything else uses dasherized names such as `embeddable-host`. The fix belongs at the store boundary. As written, `replace` without `/g` handles only the first underscore.

findings.title: Plural `_ids` branch is unguarded and applies to every REST payload
findings.description: The regex now rewrites every `*_ids` key on any `__rest_serializer` payload. Only the embedding response currently emits one, so this is a future-facing risk. `obj[k].map` assumes an array, and `_lookupSubType` returns undefined for ids missing from the root collection, which leaves `undefined` entries in the array. The singular branch guards against this with `if (hydrated)`; the plural branch does not. `hydrated || []` is dead code, because `map` always returns an array.

findings.title: Stale buffer after a successful save
findings.description: On success, the component never calls `commitBuffer()` or `rollbackBuffer()`, so the buffer keeps the typed value. If the server normalizes the host, the next `edit()` shows the un-normalized value. The impact is UI-only.

findings.title: Duplicate imports from one module
findings.description: `computed` and `{ on, observes }` are imported from `ember-addons/ember-computed-decorators` in two separate statements. Merge them.

findings.title: Naming and return-type drift around host lookup
findings.description: `record_for_host` returns `false` on some paths and nil or a record on others, so callers must handle both. `TopicEmbed.import` calls the result `eh` (app/models/topic_embed.rb:36 and :43). `spec/models/embeddable_host_spec.rb:23` is still named `allows_embeddable_host` after the method was renamed to `host_allowed?`. `spec/models/topic_spec.rb:1407` has the typo "emeddable".

findings.title: Dead and duplicated code
findings.description: The `rescue URI::InvalidURIError` is unreachable because `record_for_host` already rescues. `EmbeddableHostSerializer` redefines methods that AMS attributes already provide (app/serializers/embeddable_host_serializer.rb:1-16). Both new admin controllers repeat `before_filter :ensure_logged_in, :ensure_staff`, which `Admin::AdminController` already applies (app/controllers/admin/admin_controller.rb:3-4). `EmbeddingController` wraps its data in an `OpenStruct` rather than a real model.

findings.title: Migration hygiene
findings.description: Because the migration uses `change` and calls `execute`, it cannot be rolled back. `create_table ... force: true` (line 3) silently drops an existing table with that name. Split it into `up` and `down`, and drop `force: true`.

findings.title: Imported topics lose the configured category when no host matches
findings.description: `category:` now comes from the matched `EmbeddableHost`. If no host matches, it is nil and the topic lands uncategorized. Before this change, every imported topic went to `embed_category`. `TopicEmbed.import` is also reached from `import_remote`, which the host gate in `TopicRetriever` does not cover. This is probably intended, but it is a behavior change worth calling out.

findings.title: Host gating is an exact match on the parsed hostname
findings.description: The hostname is taken from `URI(...)` and compared with `lower(host) = ?`, which is parameterized. Referers such as `https://eviltrout.com.evil.com` and `http://eviltrout.com@evil.com` (whose host is `evil.com`) are rejected. A nil or unparseable referer returns false.

findings.title: New admin endpoints are staff-only
findings.description: The controllers inherit `Admin::AdminController`, which runs `ensure_logged_in` and `ensure_staff`. The routes also sit behind `AdminConstraint` (config/routes.rb:139 and :153).
